meta.titre: Democracy and Political Participation: why it matters and how citizens take part
meta.sous_theme: Meaning and features of democracy, and the forms of citizen participation

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: The council of a small town meets to decide whether to repair a road or to build a new market. Some residents attend and give their opinions, others complain at home, and many do not know that the meeting took place. The decision will still affect everybody. This is why democracy and participation are linked: rule by the people works only when the people take part. At the GCE you are asked why democracy is valued, what participation means and why citizens join in public life.

items: Government is the group of people and institutions that rule a country.
A citizen is a person who has rights and duties in his or her country.
An election is a process in which people choose their leaders by voting.
A political party is an organised group that seeks power in order to govern.

sections.titre: Democracy and political participation: meaning, features and ways of taking part
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Meaning
**Democracy** comes from two Greek words meaning *people* and *rule*. It is government by the people, usually described as government of the people, by the people and for the people. In **direct democracy** citizens decide themselves, as in a small meeting. In **representative democracy** citizens elect people who decide for them, such as councillors and members of parliament. Cameroon's system is representative.

### Features of a democracy
- Free and fair elections held at regular intervals.
- The rule of law: everybody, including leaders, is equal before the law.
- Fundamental freedoms of expression, association and the press.
- Several political parties and freedom to join or form one.
- Separation of powers and independent courts.
- Accountability: leaders must explain their actions.
- Rule by the majority with respect for the rights of minorities.

### Why democracy is considered the best form of government
Authority comes from the consent of the people. Leaders can be changed peacefully. Rights and freedoms are protected, citizens' views are heard and leaders are held to account.

### Political participation
This means all the ways in which citizens take part in running public affairs.
| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| Voting | Choosing councillors and other leaders |
| Standing for office | Joining a party and being a candidate |
| Taking part in local government | Attending council meetings, giving ideas, paying council dues |
| Peaceful expression | Petitions, letters, debates, lawful meetings |
| Associations | Youth groups, unions, community development associations |

**Voting** is the most basic form, because it gives leaders their authority, but participation goes beyond voting.

### Why citizens take part in council activities
Council decisions concern daily life: roads, water, markets and civil status documents. Citizens want the development of their own locality, and the council is the level of government closest to them.

### Obstacles
Lack of information, apathy, poverty, distance, fear and the belief that one's vote does not count.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says give reasons why democracy is preferred
variantes.contenu_markdown: Link each reason to a benefit for the citizen: power comes from the people, leaders can be removed peacefully, rights are protected, and everybody is equal before the law. Do not insult other forms of government.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how citizens participate
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the way, say what the citizen does, and give the result: voting, so that leaders receive authority; attending council meetings, so that local needs are heard.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks about problems and remedies
variantes.contenu_markdown: Pair each obstacle with a remedy: lack of information with civic education, distance with local meetings, apathy with awareness campaigns.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain four ways in which young people of your age can take part in the political life of Cameroon. (8 marks)

etapes.justification: Pupils may be under voting age, so the ways must be realistic for them.
etapes.resultat_markdown: School clubs and councils, civic education, community work, preparing to vote.
Join school clubs, learn about public affairs, take part in community activities, register to vote when old enough.

etapes.justification: The command word is explain, so each way needs a reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A debate club teaches members to give opinions and listen to others.

etapes.action: Check that each way is political.
etapes.justification: Political participation concerns public affairs and not only private life.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Each way links to community decisions or leaders.

etapes.justification: A final sentence ties the ways to democracy.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Young people who take part now will be able to take part well as adults.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: First, pupils can join school clubs and take part in the choice of class representatives or club leaders, which teaches them how to choose leaders. Second, they can learn about public affairs and civic education, so that they understand their rights and duties. Third, they can take part in community activities, such as cleaning campaigns, and give ideas to the local council. Fourth, when they reach the age fixed by the law, they can register and vote. Young people who take part now will be better citizens when they are adults.

items.erreur_markdown: "Democracy means that everybody can do what he or she likes."
items.pourquoi_faux: Democracy rests on the rule of law. Freedoms are used within the law and with respect for the rights of other people.
items.correction_markdown: Say that democracy gives freedom under the law.

items.erreur_markdown: "Political participation means voting and nothing else."
items.pourquoi_faux: Voting is one form. Citizens also stand for office, attend council meetings, join associations and express opinions peacefully.
items.correction_markdown: Give several forms and mention voting as the most basic.

items.erreur_markdown: "In a democracy, the majority is always right, so minority views do not matter."
items.pourquoi_faux: A democracy respects the rights of minorities and protects their freedom to speak and to take part.
items.correction_markdown: Write: majority rule with respect for the rights of minorities.

items.erreur_markdown: "Only politicians and adults take part in political life."
items.pourquoi_faux: Every citizen has a part to play, and young people can take part in school and community life and in civic activities.
items.correction_markdown: Name ways in which ordinary citizens and young people participate.

items.erreur_markdown: "A country is democratic as soon as it holds an election."
items.pourquoi_faux: Elections must be free and fair, and they must go with freedoms, the rule of law and accountability.
items.correction_markdown: Describe an election as one feature among many.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Define democracy. (b) State two features of a democratic country.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Democracy is government by the people, either directly or through representatives chosen in elections. (b) Any two: free and fair elections; rule of law; freedom of expression; several political parties; separation of powers; accountability. Award marks for the definition and one mark for each feature.

items.enonce_markdown: A town council holds a public meeting to hear what residents want, but very few people come. (a) Give two reasons why residents may stay away. (b) Suggest two ways of increasing attendance. (c) State one benefit of attending.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Any two: they were not informed; they think that their opinion will not count; they are busy with work; the venue is far; they do not trust the council. (b) Any two: announce the meeting by radio, posters and village heads; hold meetings in several neighbourhoods; explain the topics clearly; show that views are used. (c) Citizens can influence decisions that affect their daily life, or they can hold the council accountable. Award marks for each correct answer.

items.enonce_markdown: "A democracy cannot succeed if citizens vote and then take no further interest." Explain three reasons why this is so.
items.solution_markdown: Possible points: leaders need to be watched and questioned between elections, otherwise they may not be accountable; problems that need local solutions are known only if citizens speak out; laws and projects work better when citizens help and obey them; groups that are silent may be ignored. Conclusion: voting gives authority, while continuing participation makes sure that authority is used well. Award marks for three developed reasons and a conclusion.

items_markdown: Democracy is government by the people, directly or through elected representatives.
Its features include free and fair elections, the rule of law, freedoms, several parties, separation of powers and accountability.
Democracy is valued because power comes from the consent of the people and leaders can be changed peacefully.
Political participation includes voting, standing for office, taking part in council life, peaceful expression and joining associations.
Citizens take part in council activities because council decisions touch daily life and development.
Obstacles such as ignorance, apathy and distance can be reduced by civic education and awareness.
